name: Smuggler's Surprise
oracle_text:
Spree (Choose one or more additional costs.)
+ {2} — Mill four cards. You may put up to two creature and/or land cards from among the milled cards into your hand.
+ {4}{G} — You may put up to two creature cards from your hand onto the battlefield.
+ {1} — Creatures you control with power 4 or greater gain hexproof and indestructible until end of turn.
blocked_sentences: Spree (Choose one or more additional costs.)
+ {2} — Mill four cards. You may put up to two creature and/or land cards from among the milled cards into your hand.
+ {4}{G} — You may put up to two creature cards from your hand onto the battlefield.
+ {1} — Creatures you control with power 4 or greater gain hexproof and indestructible until end of turn.

needs.what: A card-level list of priced modes where the caster chooses a non-empty SUBSET of them as the spell is cast, pays the mana of every chosen mode on top of the base cost, and on resolution runs only the chosen modes' effects in printed order. Three pieces are missing: (1) a cast-time multi-select -- legality offering a cast line per payable subset, or a subset decision at cast -- and a spell that is not castable with zero modes chosen; (2) a record on the spell object of WHICH modes were paid, a SET where `StackItem.cost_option` and `CardObject.cast_cost_option` are today a single `int | None`; (3) a set-membership sibling of the `{"cost_option": n}` condition, asking whether mode n was among those paid, so each printed '+ <cost> -- <effect>' line is an `if` on its own mode. Every printed line on this card is blocked by it: the three modes exist only as riders on the spree cost and cannot be attached to their prices without it. The mode EFFECTS are each already expressible with today's vocabulary -- `mill` with `as: "milled"` then `return_from_graveyard` over that binding, `put_onto_battlefield` from hand, and `grant_keyword` over a power>=4 selector -- so closing this gap should turn the card straight into an ordinary answer.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `additional_cost_options` is the closest thing and is exclusive by construction: the loader calls it 'a choice between prices' and refuses fewer than two, `chosen_additional()` in src/automtg/engine/casting.py returns `card.additional_cost_options[choice]` for exactly one index, `_charge_additional_cost` builds one cast line per single branch, and the paid branch is stored as one `int | None`, so `{"cost_option": n}` can only ever report a single mode. Spelling Smuggler's Surprise that way would let the player pay exactly one of the three prices and never two -- a strictly different, much weaker card. `kicker` plus `additional_repeatable`/`multikicker` is one fixed price paid N times, not three distinct prices with three distinct effects, and the loader explicitly refuses `additional_repeatable` beside `additional_cost_options`. `choose_mode` does pick a subset, but it runs at RESOLUTION, so (per the note beside `additional_cost_options` in src/automtg/cards/schema.py) it can neither be a cost nor decide whether the spell is castable -- writing the three modes as a `choose_mode` would hand the player all three for {G} with the prices never charged. `additional_optional` only makes one fixed price skippable.
